sluzby.titulek: Seven disciplines, one point of responsibility
sluzby.lead: You don't have to put together a designer, an installation company, and a service provider yourself. We manage the entire chain — and when something goes wrong two years from now, you call the same number.

postup.lead: Four steps, no surprises. At each stage you know what you get and who is responsible for it.

servis.popis: We take over regular maintenance, inspections, and checks. After an agreed period we verify whether the system is delivering the promised savings.

energetika.kratky: Certificates, energy audits, mandatory inspections per Decree 38/2022 Coll., and refits.
energetika.titulek: Energy performance certificates, energy audits, and refits
energetika.lead: We value your energy. We measure, calculate, and tell you what makes sense to change — and what doesn't.
energetika.popis: Our energy specialist prepares energy performance certificates and energy audits, carries out mandatory inspections of operating systems, and proposes a refit that does not start with demolishing the plant room.

body.b1: Preparation of energy performance certificates in accordance with the Energy Act; registered in the ENEX database (Ministry of Industry and Trade)
body.b2: Inspection of operating systems per Decree 38/2022 Coll. for heat sources above 70 kW
body.b3: Energy audit per Act No. 406/2000 Coll. and Decree No. 480/2012 Coll., always at least two variants
body.b5: Diagnostics of heating systems, cooling systems, and HVAC
body.b6: System balancing per Decree 193/2007 Coll. including flow rate setting protocol
body.b7: Inspection of pressure vessels and gas appliances
body.b8: Indoor air quality measurement — thermal comfort, CO₂, TVOC

upozorneni.popis: Per the update effective 1 January 2023, the owner is obligated to have an energy specialist carry out an inspection of operating systems once every 5 years. Failure to comply may result in a fine of up to CZK 200,000.

refit.popis: Our philosophy is sustainability. After the audit, we propose which parts of the system can be retained and which should be replaced with newer, more efficient units compliant with current standards. The result is lower investment and a smaller environmental impact.

k1.popis: We walk through the building, meter readings, documentation, and actual operation — not just design values.

k2.popis: We prepare an assessment of the current energy performance and propose at least two optimization variants.

k3.popis: We evaluate the variants economically and environmentally and recommend the most suitable one — with justification.

k4.popis: We can also implement the measures and, after an agreed period, verify that the savings have actually materialized.

eac-filtry.lead: We are the Honeywell partner for the Czech Republic in the field of special EAC filters. They capture fine dust while reducing HVAC energy consumption.
eac-filtry.popis: The electronic air cleaner captures harmful PM2.5 particles and has a significantly lower pressure drop than a standard filter. The fan does not have to work as hard — and that shows on the invoice.

body.b2: Lower pressure drop than a standard filter — approximately 5% savings in AHU fan power

body.b4: Washable pre-filter and collector — lower operating costs, environmentally friendly

vymeniky.lead: A cracked heat exchanger does not necessarily mean a new one. We diagnose, repair, and test — often at a fraction of the replacement cost.
vymeniky.popis: We have our own facility with test tanks and helium testing, so we can detect leaks that a water pressure test would miss.

d-tepelna-cerpadla.lead: We calculate whether it pays off for your property, design the capacity, install it — and handle the subsidy application for you.
d-tepelna-cerpadla.popis: A heat pump is not a universal solution for every home. Before we recommend one, we calculate heat losses and assess the existing heating system. d-rekuperace.kratky: Controlled ventilation with heat recovery for new builds and renovated apartments.
d-rekuperace.lead: Fresh air without open windows — and without heating the street in winter.
d-rekuperace.popis: Heat recovery returns heat from exhaust air back into the building. In practice, this means you can ventilate continuously without using more heating than before. It works best during construction or renovation, but we can install it in a completed apartment as well.

body.b1: Central units and local heat recovery for individual rooms
body.b2: Duct design that fits within ceiling voids without lowering the ceiling more than necessary

logisticke-centrum-d1.zadani: The operator of a logistics park wanted to reduce heating costs for the warehouses and administrative section. The original plan was to replace the entire boiler room.

d-rodinny-dum-cerpadlo.nazev: Heat pump replacing a gas boiler
d-rodinny-dum-cerpadlo.perex: An older house with radiators. Instead of a quick source replacement, we first calculated the losses and modified the system — otherwise the heat pump would have been running expensively.
d-rodinny-dum-cerpadlo.zadani: The owners wanted to move away from gas. The house has original radiators designed for high water temperatures, which is exactly the situation where a heat pump alone will not deliver savings.

rozsah.r1: Heat loss calculation and heating system assessment
rozsah.r2: Replacement of two undersized radiators so the system could operate at a lower temperature
rozsah.r3: Air-to-water heat pump in a cascade with bivalent backup heating
rozsah.r4: Connection to domestic hot water heating and the storage tank
rozsah.r5: Hydraulic balancing of the system and grant processing under power of attorney

d-rodinny-dum-cerpadlo.vysledek: After the first winter we returned and fine-tuned the equithermal curve based on actual operation. The system now runs at a lower water temperature than originally designed, and the heat pump maintains a good heating factor.

d-byt-rekuperace.nazev: Heat recovery for an apartment after renovation
d-byt-rekuperace.perex: Apartment in a masonry building after a full renovation. The ductwork had to fit within the already-designed suspended ceilings.
d-byt-rekuperace.zadani: The owners wanted ventilation without opening windows onto a noisy street. The renovation was already underway, so the only space left for ductwork was within the suspended ceilings.

rozsah.r1: Survey of the layout and verification of available space in the suspended ceilings
rozsah.r2: Design of air volumes for individual rooms
rozsah.r3: Central heat recovery unit in the utility room
rozsah.r4: Ductwork with flat ducts and noise attenuators at the unit
rozsah.r5: Flow balancing at the diffusers including a protocol report

d-byt-rekuperace.vysledek: The apartment is ventilated continuously without windows open onto the street. Unit noise remained below the level audible in living spaces.

d-vymena-kotle.nazev: Emergency boiler replacement during heating season
d-vymena-kotle.perex: A call to the dispatch centre in January: no heating. The old boiler was beyond repair; the new one arrived within two days.
d-vymena-kotle.zadani: A customer called the 24/7 dispatch centre to report that her boiler had stopped heating. During the inspection, it became clear that repair was no longer viable — parts lead times exceeded the time it would take to replace the unit.

rozsah.r1: Same-day site visit and fault diagnosis
rozsah.r2: Design of the replacement heat source and on-site quotation
rozsah.r3: Dismantling and removal of the old boiler
rozsah.r4: Installation of a new condensing boiler including flue modification
rozsah.r5: Commissioning, training, and entry into the inspection log

d-vymena-kotle.vysledek: Two days elapsed from the phone call to full heating, one of which was waiting for boiler delivery. The household was without heat for one night.

pribeh.p1: We are a team of experienced employees, many of whom have over 25 years of practice in building services engineering. We draw on both this experience and new insights from an industry that continues to evolve dynamically.
pribeh.p2: We operate from Prague and a branch in Milevsko. Our primary clients are companies and operators of office buildings, shopping centres, hospitals, museums, galleries, and public facilities — but we also install air conditioning in residential homes when it makes sense.
pribeh.p3: What we enjoy most: when a demanding client's clear vision meets the skill of our technicians.

h2.popis: Permanent employees with certified tools, which we train on continuously. Not a crew of subcontractors you see for the first time.

napsali-o-nas.nazev: They Wrote About Us: Interview for Eko-Adepto
napsali-o-nas.perex: The independent Eko-Adepto project visited us in person and documented what we told them about the company, technologies, and maintenance.
napsali-o-nas.text: Representatives of the Eko-Adepto project visited us in person and walked through our offered technologies, how the company operates, maintenance, and the team's experience. In the article you will find what we truly focus on: building services for larger buildings — offices, shopping centres, hospitals, museums and galleries, and public facilities. Households make up a smaller share of our projects, but we also install air conditioning, heat pumps, and heat recovery for them.

klimatizace-bungalovu.nazev: Air Conditioning for a Bungalow Without a Single Trim Strip
klimatizace-bungalovu.perex: The client wanted design indoor units and a clean interior with no visible trim strips for refrigerant piping. Three site visits and grooves in the masonry solved it.
klimatizace-bungalovu.text: After the offer was approved, the team headed to the site and precisely marked out the routes for grooves in the masonry. On the second visit, we laid the piping, cabling, and condensate drainage into the prepared grooves and routed them through the floor to the outdoor unit location — it was a multi-split system with three indoor units and one outdoor unit. The customer then had the grooves plastered over and painted. On the third visit, we installed the units, commissioned the system, tested it, and explained the complete operation including the phone app.

kontrola-38-2022.nazev: Have you completed the mandatory inspection under Decree 38/2022 Coll.?
kontrola-38-2022.perex: Per the update effective 1 January 2023, the owner must have an inspection of operated systems carried out once every 5 years. The penalty for non-compliance can reach up to CZK 200,000.
kontrola-38-2022.text: The obligation applies to buildings with heat sources exceeding 70 kW, including those outside buildings. The inspection of operated systems — HVAC, heating, cooling, and cogeneration units — may only be performed by a certified energy specialist and is recorded in the ENEX database, administered by the Ministry of Industry and Trade. We will arrange this for you, including follow-up diagnostics, system balancing per Decree 193/2007 Coll., and pressure vessel inspections.

nabor-techniku.nazev: We are hiring HVAC service technicians
nabor-techniku.perex: We are expanding our service division. We are looking for technicians with an interest in HVAC, cooling, or heating — experience is a plus, but willingness to learn is equally valued.
nabor-techniku.text: We offer a dedicated service vehicle, complete certified equipment, ongoing manufacturer training, and a team environment where you can always ask for help. We mostly work in pairs across Prague, central Bohemia, and southern Bohemia. Get in touch via our Careers page or directly with the service department manager.

firemni-den-systemair.nazev: Systemair company day in České Budějovice
firemni-den-systemair.perex: As part of our employee product training, we attended a company day hosted by Systemair.
firemni-den-systemair.text: We would like to thank our partners at Systemair for sharing new industry insights and for the enjoyable time during the leisure portion of the programme. We take the product training of our technicians seriously — on site, it becomes clear who truly knows the equipment.

panelova-diskuze-cvut.nazev: Panel discussion on heat pumps at CTU
panelova-diskuze-cvut.perex: We took part in a panel discussion on heat pumps at the Czech Technical University in Prague.
panelova-diskuze-cvut.text: The debate centred on the real-world efficiency of heat pumps in our climate conditions, the design of bivalent heat sources, and the gap between design assumptions and actual operation. These are exactly the discrepancies we encounter on site, and we are happy to discuss them with the professional community.

rozsireni-servisu.perex: Our service division has added an energy specialist, system diagnostics, and heat exchanger repairs at our own facility.
rozsireni-servisu.text: We now offer EPC and energy assessments, technical reports on the inspection of operated systems, balancing of heating and cooling systems including protocols, and indoor air quality measurements. We have also added repair and refurbishment of damaged or cracked heat exchangers — with diagnostics, repair, and testing in immersion tanks or by helium pressure testing.

stranka.lead: In our industry, few people go easy on abbreviations. Here they are explained — and wherever you come across one on the site, just hover over or tap it.
stranka.hledat: Search for an abbreviation or term
stranka.nenalezeno: We don't have that abbreviation yet. Ask us.

TZB.popis: A collective term for HVAC, heating, cooling, sanitary installations, gas, and measurement and control — everything that distributes heat, cold, air, and water in a building.

VZT.popis: A system that supplies fresh air to a building, extracts stale air, and along the way filters, heats, or cools it.

ZTI.popis: Water supply, drainage, and fixtures in a building.

MaR.popis: Sensors, controllers, and a control system that maintain set values — temperature, humidity, flow rate — without human intervention.

BMS.popis: A supervisory system for the building. It collects data from all systems, monitors alarms, and allows operation to be managed from a single point.

PENB.full: energy performance certificate of a building
PENB.popis: A mandatory document assessing the energy performance of a building. It is prepared by an energy specialist and registered in the ENEX database.

ENEX.popis: A registry of certificates, audits, and assessments managed by the Ministry of Industry and Trade.

MPO.popis: The central authority responsible for energy legislation and the ENEX database.

BIM.popis: A design approach where instead of drawing lines you model real elements with properties. From the model you can extract schedules, clash detection, and documentation for building management.

TČ.popis: A device that transfers heat from outdoor air, the ground, or water into the heating system. For every kilowatt-hour of electricity it delivers several kilowatt-hours of heat.

EAC.popis: A filter that charges dust particles and captures them on collector plates. Compared to a conventional filter cartridge, it has a lower pressure drop and can be washed.

AHU.popis: The mechanical heart of ventilation: fans, filters, heat exchangers, and heat recovery in a single cabinet. In English, air handling unit.

ZZT.popis: Recovery. Outgoing warm air transfers its heat to incoming fresh air — without the two streams mixing.

PM2,5.popis: Particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres. They penetrate deep into the lungs, which is why the purpose of filtration is to capture precisely these.

TVOC.popis: A collective indicator of gaseous organic compounds in indoor air — from furniture, adhesives, paints, and cleaning products. Measured when assessing indoor air quality.

KJ.popis: A device that produces electricity and heat simultaneously. Fuel utilisation is significantly higher than with electricity generation alone.

PBŘ.popis: Part of the documentation specifying fire resistance, escape routes, and the behaviour of ventilation systems in the event of a fire.

TNS.popis: A vessel operating under pressure for which regulations require periodic inspections — typically expansion vessels and storage tanks.

COP.popis: The ratio of heat delivered to electricity consumed at a given moment. A COP of 4 means four kilowatt-hours of heat for every one kilowatt-hour of electricity.

SCOP.popis: Heating coefficient averaged over an entire heating season. A fairer metric than COP for comparing heat pumps.

EER.popis: The ratio of cooling capacity to electrical power consumed.

VRF.popis: Air conditioning system in which a single outdoor unit serves multiple indoor units, with refrigerant flow controlled according to the actual demand of each unit.

DSP.popis: Design stage used by the building authority to assess the construction project.

DPS.popis: Detailed design stage used as the basis for actual on-site installation.

RDS.popis: Documentation prepared by the contractor for its own execution, building upon the construction execution documentation.

TDS.popis: A specialist representing the investor's interests on site — monitors quality, scope, and compliance with the design.

ČSN.popis: National technical standard. Specifies requirements such as fresh air volume, noise levels, or equipment safety.

HVAC.popis: English abbreviation for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning. The international equivalent of the Czech term TZB.
